newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek storms float scores of cars through streets.
newsitem.headline: Greek storms float scores of cars through streets.

text.p: Heavy storms on Sunday sent scores of cars floating like toy boats through streets in towns around Greece and caused extensive damage to homes and shops.
Live television reports from Corinth, west of Athens, showed dozens of empty cars floating swiftly through the main streets, which had been turned into raging rivers.
Rail lines and streets around Athens were heavily flooded and water a metre (several feet) deep churned through suburbs and central intersections.
The northern suburb of Kifissia in Athens was awash, with water lapping against windows of fashionable boutiques.
Police said Corinth and villages around the Peleponnese peninsula were particularly hard hit. Heavy damage was also reported in Athens and in northern regions around the port of Salonika.
